items.stem: In Maven, which dependency scope means the dependency is available at compile time but is expected to be provided by the runtime container and is NOT packaged?

options.rationale: Correct: provided dependencies are on the compile classpath but not bundled; the container supplies them.
compile is the default and IS packaged into the artifact.
runtime dependencies are packaged; they just are not needed at compile time.
import applies only to dependencyManagement BOMs, not to a normal dependency at runtime.

items.explanation: Correct: provided dependencies are on the compile classpath but not bundled; the container supplies them.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the Gradle build correctly distinguish the configuration phase from the execution phase? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Code in a task's doLast block runs during the execution phase
options.rationale: Correct: doLast/doFirst actions run at execution.

options.text: Top-level code in build.gradle runs during the configuration phase
options.rationale: Correct: the build script body is evaluated while the task graph is configured.

options.text: The configuration phase runs only the tasks requested on the command line
options.rationale: All projects are configured regardless of which tasks were requested (without configuration avoidance).

items.explanation: Correct: doLast/doFirst actions run at execution.

items.stem: A build must produce byte-for-byte identical artifacts across machines. Which practice most undermines that goal?

options.rationale: Correct: SNAPSHOT resolves to the latest build and changes over time, so outputs are not reproducible.
The wrapper pins the Gradle version, which helps reproducibility.

options.text: Importing a BOM to fix versions
options.rationale: A BOM fixes versions, aiding reproducibility.
The cache reuses identical outputs; it does not make them differ.

items.explanation: Correct: SNAPSHOT resolves to the latest build and changes over time, so outputs are not reproducible.
